status: Attempted route ruled out for required ordered-object result guarantee; source-only finding, no new candidate.
question: Can public scripting.executeScript MAIN run the original page Program once and let background host code preserve its completion JSON order?
conclusion: Files can execute a page Program. But completion has already become native Foundation id before resultJSON encoding, is parsed into ObjC containers again, and only then projected to background JS. It is not end-to-end SerializedScriptValue or original ordered JSON delivery. This cannot provide the required property-order contract.

callChain.finding: Public details accepts resource files or func, not both. Func must be a function, converted to function.toString; no original lexical closure crosses.
MAIN selects the page Main content-world enum.
Loaded privileged extension, scripting permission, actual tab and URL/tab access are checked before resolving source pairs/world.
Selects frames/documents and checks frame permission. Func is return(function)(...arguments) via async function. Files use native page-world Program evaluation, retaining that distinction.
Both branches already return native id resultOfExecution, not an opaque original JS value.
Encodes native id as internal resultJSON, with frame/document identifiers and error string.
Parses internal resultJSON back into Objective-C value; puts it into NSMutableDictionary result. Raw original JSON is not a public return field.
Public callback receives toJSValueRef(globalContext,toWebAPI(...)); background serialization happens after these projections.

reusedBoundary.finding: Engine native internal entrypoints distinguish Program and async function. Referencing these sources is not app authorization to call private API.
Native Program source is evaluated directly in the selected world, not through page eval.
JS object properties are extracted into a dictionary container before native reconstruction; original JS property ordering is not a public dictionary guarantee.

counterexamples.kind: Transport-contract distinction, not observed SDK reordering
counterexamples.meaning: These share the native dictionary key/value mapping but require different JSON order. Foundation encode/parse/toJS does not promise to preserve that distinction. Passing one sample would not prove the required general contract.

counterexamples.kind: Program versus func semantics, not executed here
counterexamples.meaning: Func wrapping yields undefined unless a return is inserted and keeps declarations function-local. Inserting a return still changes declaration lifetime. Files avoid that wrapper, but not the failed ordered-result transport.

CSP.scope: Not expanded after the transport failure, per Root instruction. Files call native page-world Program execution; no eval/CSP bypass or shipped-platform CSP equivalence is claimed.

errorsAndOwnership: Native localized execution errors become per-injection error strings; frame denial also becomes a result. Frames/file callbacks are asynchronously aggregated. This is not proof of existing App source revision/page lease/cancellation/drain semantics.

availability.limit: Actual SDK/host option support is unexecuted.

proofLimits: No actual WK order loss was measured; the negative conclusion concerns the transport contract, not a claim that every sample is reordered.
No author Program executed in an extension background or new VM/JSContext. No runtime tests or new candidate.
This does not rule out legitimate unrelated uses of the scripting API.
The separate single-expression page-encoding characterization still awaits real WK tests and is not arbitrary Program support.
